lines.text: Same mountain. One eruption rated a two, the other rated a five.
This is Mount St. Helens, from 2004 to 2008.
For more than three years, lava kept squeezing up and building a new dome in the crater.
By July 2007, that dome was ninety-three million cubic metres. On the official scale, the eruption rates a two.
Now the same mountain, on the eighteenth of May, 1980. This is real film, shot from a plane.
About one cubic kilometre of ash, over nine hours. That rates a five.
Three years, a two. Nine hours, a five. So what made the difference? That's level two, and the full video is linked right here.
